blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — aprepitant and dexamethasone drug interaction
stem: An adult client is prescribed the standard 3-day oral aprepitant regimen for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting prevention together with oral dexamethasone. Which dexamethasone adjustment is expected because of the aprepitant interaction?

options.A: Reduce the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50% because the 3-day aprepitant regimen increases dexamethasone exposure.
options.B: Increase the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50% because aprepitant lowers dexamethasone exposure during the standard 3-day regimen.
options.C: Use the usual dexamethasone dose without adjustment because aprepitant does not produce a clinically meaningful interaction with oral dexamethasone.
options.D: Stop dexamethasone completely because coadministration with aprepitant is contraindicated rather than managed with a dose adjustment.

rationale: Current aprepitant labeling states that the standard 3-day aprepitant regimen increases dexamethasone exposure. The drug-interaction table directs clinicians to reduce the dose of oral dexamethasone by approximately 50%, and the CINV dosing tables likewise incorporate a 50% dexamethasone reduction to account for the interaction. Therefore A is correct. B reverses the direction of the interaction, C denies a labeled clinically relevant exposure increase, and D incorrectly treats dexamethasone as contraindicated with aprepitant.
educational_objective: Recognize the clinically significant aprepitant-dexamethasone interaction and the labeled recommendation to reduce oral dexamethasone by approximately 50% during the standard 3-day aprepitant regimen.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label dated June 11, 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Dosage and Administration §2.1 CINV dosing tables/footnotes: 50% dexamethasone dosage reduction to account for interaction; Drug Interactions §7.1, Dexamethasone: increased dexamethasone exposure; with 3-day aprepitant regimen reduce oral dexamethasone by approximately 50%. Current DailyMed lines 369-400 and 585-590.
source_claim_supported: The 3-day aprepitant regimen increases dexamethasone exposure and the label recommends reducing oral dexamethasone by approximately 50%.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: identify medication interactions, review pertinent data, and monitor/evaluate medication therapy.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete interaction-management strategies without absolute-word distractor cues.
Preserved the exact label-supported approximately-50% dose reduction and balanced option length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current aprepitant labeling. B reverses the interaction, C denies it, and D incorrectly labels the combination contraindicated; the numeric adjustment is directly source-supported.
